text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Opus
text: Three games running, the killers won because this table votes on vibes and buries whoever claims to know something. Let's fix that tonight.

Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.

text: I'm proud my officer claim on Opus was accurate from the start—even killed early, that information carried the table to the right finish.

name: Haiku
text: Proud I caught Terra matching Opus's votes both days. Regret leaning so hard on that pattern alone. I was loud, right, and too sure of myself.

name: Gemma
text: I told you my death would hand them the win, and you all fell for it until it was too late.

name: Sol
text: I regret voting out Gemma, but I’m glad I followed the case against Terra when it mattered.

name: Luna
text: I’m proud we turned the cards over and caught both killers, though I let suspicion of Terra outrun the proof.

name: Terra
text: I regret voting Sonnet when Gemma’s flip had already made Opus’s officer story collapse.

name: Opus
text: Claiming the badge first was the move; naming a citizen as my target was the mistake, and my last swing at Haiku just made Terra look cleaner than me.

Opus and Sonnet both claimed to be the officer on Day 1, and Opus named Gemma while Sonnet named Opus. The town voted out Gemma that day, and she showed citizen, which made Opus's claim look shaky. On Night 2 the doctor saved the target, so nobody died, and on Day 2 the town voted out Opus, who showed killer and named Haiku as his partner. On Night 3 the killers took Sonnet, and on Day 3 Haiku pushed the town to vote out Terra, the last killer, based on her votes. The town won with every killer out, and the roles were Sonnet the officer, Haiku the doctor, Terra and Opus the killers, and Gemma, Sol, and Luna the citizens.
